kjv: the form of the fourth is like the Son of God
mine: the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods
note: bar-elahin (plural, no article) on a pagan king's lips means "a divine being", which he calls "his angel" in 3:28; KJV's capitalised "the Son of God" reads a christological title into it.

kjv: cornet, flute, harp, sackbut, psaltery, dulcimer
mine: horn, pipe, lyre, trigon, harp, bagpipe
note: qatros (Greek kitharis), sabbekha (Greek sambyke, a triangular harp), pesanterin (psalterion) and sumponyah are Greek instrument names; "sackbut" (a trombone) and "dulcimer" are anachronistic European instruments.
